subject: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>; Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>; Hanae Suzuki <hanae_suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 9:14 AM PT
Subject: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)

Hi Marcus/Kevin/Hanae,

We’re trying to lock “secure-by-default” posture language + defaults for the Private VPC Terraform modules alpha this week (ENG-4852 / ENG-4829). Can you review/confirm the proposed audit logging defaults and IAM boundary approach below?

Scope: networking + foundational infra only (VPC/subnets/endpoints/logging/IAM scaffolding). Installer/Helm handles cluster/app install.

1) Audit logging defaults (proposal)
- VPC Flow Logs: enabled by default at VPC level; capture=ALL.
- Destination: CloudWatch Logs by default (customer account), with optional S3 destination (customer-owned bucket) if preferred.
- CW log group name: /redwood/private/vpc-flow-logs/${var.env}
- Retention: 90 days default (configurable), encrypted w/ customer KMS key if provided.
- If S3 destination: bucket must be customer-owned; module can create bucket only if explicitly opted-in; default is “bring your own bucket” to avoid accidental public policies.

2) DNS / endpoint-related logging (proposal)
- We are NOT turning on Route 53 Resolver Query Logging by default in alpha (cost/complexity), but we want a documented extension point.
- We do want a “minimum endpoint set” documented + preflighted by installer: ECR (api + dkr), S3 gateway, STS, CloudWatch Logs, EC2, KMS (tbd list from Victor/Nina).

3) Customer-facing security posture statements (draft)
- “By default, all logs are stored in the customer’s AWS account. Redwood does not require direct access to log destinations.”
- “All resources are private by default; public subnets exist only to support NAT gateways when required for controlled egress.”
- “No inbound access is opened to the internet by default; ingress is expected via customer-managed connectivity (VPN/DX) or internal LB patterns.”

4) IAM boundary approach (proposal)
- Module creates an installer execution role scaffold (optional) with a required permission boundary input.
- We will ship a recommended boundary policy template (customer-managed) that allows necessary actions in scoped resource ARNs (VPC, endpoints, log group, EKS prereqs where needed) and blocks IAM wildcard escalation.
- Requirement: if customer opts into role creation, they MUST provide boundary ARN (fail fast).

Asks:
A) Approve or suggest changes to retention default + destinations.
B) Confirm whether we should make Flow Logs destination default CloudWatch vs S3 (I’ve seen enterprise preference both ways).
C) Confirm language that we can safely ship for alpha re: “least privilege” and “no Redwood access.”

Attachments:
- private-vpc-logging-defaults-v0.3.pdf
- installer-execution-role-boundary-proposal-v1.docx

Thanks,
Naomi
Security & Compliance PM
Redwood Inference


---
From: Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>; Hanae Suzuki <hanae_suzuki@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)

+1 on Flow Logs enabled by default w/ ALL traffic.

On destination:
- For “works out of the box,” CloudWatch is the least-friction default. S3 introduces bucket policy/KMS gotchas + cross-account delivery questions.
- But we should explicitly support S3 because SIEM pipelines often prefer it.

Retention:
- 90d default is fine for alpha. Make sure the doc says “set to your policy requirements” and we don’t imply compliance coverage.

DNS logging:
- Agree not defaulting Resolver Query Logging in alpha; it’s noisy and expensive. Please add a doc section on how to enable and where it fits (query logs can help w/ the exact failure modes we’re seeing in pilots).

Customer-facing posture:
- “All logs stored in the customer’s account” is good, but I’d tweak to: “By default, logs are delivered to customer-owned destinations in the customer AWS account.”
- “Redwood does not require direct access” ok; avoid “Redwood will never access” because PS sometimes gets temporary access in escalations (rare, but happens). Maybe: “Redwood does not require ongoing access; any access is customer-controlled and explicitly approved.”

Kevin
(Security Engineering - Audit Logging/SIEM)


---
From: Hanae Suzuki <hanae_suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>; Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 11:09 AM PT
Subject: Re: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)

Reviewed the IAM boundary proposal doc.

Main feedback:
1) Strongly support “boundary ARN required” (fail fast). Also require explicit acknowledgment variable if we’re going to include any IAM:* at all (even scoped). Ideally boundary denies iam:CreatePolicyVersion, iam:SetDefaultPolicyVersion, iam:AttachRolePolicy unless explicitly allowed.

2) Please avoid shipping a boundary policy that “looks permissive” even if we say it’s a template. Recommend we publish:
- a minimal boundary policy for the Terraform module execution role (create VPC resources/endpoints/log groups), and
- a separate set of policies/roles expected for installer runtime (which may be broader).

3) Customer-facing language: don’t say “least privilege” unless we define what that means in alpha. Suggest:
- “permission boundary supported by default”
- “scoped policies with clearly documented required permissions”

4) Log encryption: make sure CW log group encryption is explicitly supported via kms_key_id input; default to AWS-managed key if not provided.

Hanae
Security Engineering

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>; Hanae Suzuki <hanae_suzuki@redwoodinference.com>; Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 12:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)

Adding a couple security posture points.

Logging defaults:
- Flow Logs enabled by default is a good bar.
- If we default to CloudWatch Logs, ensure the module:
  a) creates log group with retention set (don’t rely on account defaults)
  b) uses a dedicated IAM role for flow logs delivery with minimal permissions
  c) supports kms_key_id for log group encryption

IAM boundaries:
- Agree with Hanae: we should not market “least privilege” as a guarantee in alpha.
- Put the boundary + expected permissions in docs as “Redwood-validated baseline,” and keep the actual enforcement in boundary + policy examples.

Customer posture statements:
- I suggest we add one more sentence explicitly stating:
  “No resources are publicly routable by default; if a customer enables public ingress/egress, it is an explicit configuration choice.”

Also +1 to Kevin’s suggestion: avoid “never access.” Say “no standing access required” + “customer-approved, time-bound access if needed for support.”

Marcus
Security Engineering Lead

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>; Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>; Hanae Suzuki <hanae_suzuki@redwoodinference.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 2:03 PM PT
Subject: Re: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)

This is helpful, thanks all.

Implementation notes / what we can commit to for alpha:
- CloudWatch default for Flow Logs (we already have this mostly in PR draft). S3 as optional destination behind an explicit input.
- Dedicated flow logs IAM role + kms_key_id support: we can do.
- Boundary ARN required: yes (we’ll make it a validation error).

Re: “two sets of roles”:
- Agree with Hanae: module execution role (Terraform apply) should be separate from installer runtime role. We’re already moving that direction (Victor/Bruno have separate modules). We’ll align docs accordingly.

Naomi — if you can consolidate the customer-facing statements into a paragraph we can drop into:
- module README (security posture section)
- docs quickstart (alpha disclaimer)

Irene
Infrastructure Engineering

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>; Kevin Osei <kevin_osei@redwoodinference.com>; Hanae Suzuki <hanae_suzuki@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>; Victor Alvarez <victor_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>; Allison Grant <allison_grant@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jun 10, 2025 at 4:48 PM PT
Subject: Re: Logging + IAM defaults for Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha)

Got it — I’ll incorporate the edits.

Updated posture text (draft, for README + quickstart):

“Redwood’s Private VPC Terraform modules are designed to be secure-by-default for enterprise environments. By default, VPC Flow Logs are enabled and delivered to customer-owned log destinations in the customer AWS account (CloudWatch Logs by default; S3 optional). The modules do not require standing Redwood access to customer infrastructure; any support access is customer-controlled and explicitly approved. No internet-exposed inbound access is opened by default. Public subnets are created only when required to support controlled egress (e.g., NAT gateways), and enabling public ingress/egress is an explicit configuration choice.”

IAM language (draft):

“The modules support permission boundaries and ship with Redwood-validated example policies/templates to help customers implement scoped permissions. For alpha, customers are expected to review and adapt policy templates to align with internal security requirements.”

Next steps:
- I’ll update the Confluence guidance pages and link them from the module repo.
- Irene/Victor: please ensure the module docs clearly distinguish ‘Terraform apply role’ vs ‘installer runtime role’.
- Kevin: I’ll add a short note about Resolver Query Logging as an extension point.

Thanks again.

Naomi
